prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that periodically reads moisture levels from a DFRobot Soil Moisture Sensor v2.0, an analog resistive sensor, via an MCP3008 analog-to-digital converter connected over the SPI bus. Wire the MCP3008 to the Pi's hardware SPI0 bus: chip enable CE0 on GPIO8, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9, and SCLK on GPIO11, with the sensor's analog output wired to MCP3008 channel 0 (CH0). Use the pigpio library for all SPI communication with the ADC. Sample the raw 10-bit ADC value, in the range 0-1023, once per second, and log each reading to the console together with a timestamp so the moisture trend can be reviewed later. Implement robust error handling around SPI initialization and every SPI transfer, reporting any failure rather than silently continuing. Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM for a graceful shutdown, making sure the SPI handle is closed and pigpio is terminated cleanly on every exit path, including early failures.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that reads current from an MLX91219 Hall-effect current sensor, which has an analog output, via an ADS1115 analog-to-digital converter over I2C, using the pigpio library for all I2C communication. Wire the ADS1115's ADDR pin to GND, giving it I2C address 0x48 on bus 1; wire the MLX91219's analog output to the ADS1115's AIN0 input; and wire the ADS1115's SDA and SCL lines to the Pi's GPIO2 and GPIO3. Configure the ADS1115 for single-shot mode, AIN0 single-ended (MUX=100), a programmable gain amplifier setting of PGA ±4.096V, and a data rate of 128 samples per second. Every 500ms, log the computed current in amperes to the console, deriving it from the MLX91219's sensitivity of 40mV/A with its zero-current offset centered at mid-supply. Access the ADS1115's 16-bit registers with i2cWriteI2CBlockData and i2cReadI2CBlockData, respecting the correct byte order, and handle I2C write and read errors as well as sensor-absent paths gracefully rather than crashing. On SIGINT, close the I2C handle and call gpioTerminate() before exiting.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to interface with an AZDelivery KY-026 Flame Sensor Module and an MCP3008 ADC via SPI, using the pigpio library only (do not use wiringPi). Read the KY-026 digital output (D0) on GPIO4 (BCM numbering) and sample its analog output (A0) on MCP3008 channel 0 (single-ended); connect the MCP3008 to SPI0 (CE0/GPIO8) at 1 MHz. Approximate ambient temperature from the analog reading using a linear map of the 10-bit ADC value (0-1023) to 10-40°C. Once per second, log timestamped CSV rows (Timestamp,FlameDetected,Temperature) to flame_data.csv. Implement robust error handling: verify pigpio initialization, SPI open/transfer, and file operations; on sensor-absent or SPI-failure paths, skip the log entry and print a diagnostic. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including SIGINT.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that monitors two sensors and activates a buzzer when both indicate a fire condition simultaneously, using the pigpio library for all GPIO and I2C access. Connect a Keyes KY-026 Flame Sensor's digital output to GPIO4, using the internal pull-up resistor; the sensor outputs LOW when a flame is detected. Connect an LM393-based Heat Sensor's analog output to an ADS1115 ADC on I2C bus 1 at address 0x48, channel AIN0 (single-ended), configured for single-shot mode, gain ±4.096V, 128 SPS (conversion time ~8.5ms); map the ADC voltage range 0V-3.3V linearly to 20°C-80°C and treat above 60°C as a trigger. Connect the buzzer to GPIO27, active HIGH. Poll the flame sensor and read the temperature every 100ms. Implement a 50ms debounce on the flame sensor using a falling-edge ISR callback, registering a flame event only if at least 50ms have elapsed since the last accepted event. If both a debounced flame event and temperature above 60°C occur together, log the event with a timestamp to fire_log.txt and sound the buzzer for 2 seconds. If only flame is detected, log "Flame detected!"; if only the temperature exceeds 60°C, log the temperature reading. If the ADC read fails (I2C error or sensor absent), log an error and continue without crashing. Check the return values of pigpio initialization, I2C open, the ADC configuration write, the ADC read, and log file creation, printing descriptive errors to stderr for each failure path; on any initialization failure, release all resources acquired so far and exit with code 1. Handle SIGINT by setting a running flag to 0 so the main loop exits cleanly, then turn off the buzzer, deregister the ISR, close the I2C handle, close the log file, and call gpioTerminate(). Use only pigpio, never wiringPi or libgpiod; drive the buzzer with a simple digital write rather than PWM; and ensure the code compiles cleanly with gcc -Wall, with no undeclared identifiers or implicit declarations.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 to interface with a Melexis MLX91219 current sensor (SOIC8 package, -40°C to 125°C range), which provides an analog output proportional to measured current. Read the analog signal via an external MCP3008 10-bit ADC (VREF = 3.3 V) on SPI0 CE0 (spidev0.0, GPIO8, SPI channel 0) at 1 MHz, SPI mode 0, 8 bits per word, using spidev for SPI access; read single-ended channel 0 with the 3-byte SPI command (0x01, 0x80, 0x00) and extract the 10-bit result as ((rx[1] & 0x03) << 8) | rx[2]. Convert the ADC voltage to current using the sensor sensitivity (default 100 mV/A, configurable via -s). If the measured current exceeds a configurable threshold (default 5.0 A, configurable via -t), drive GPIO18 HIGH to turn on a cooling fan; otherwise drive it LOW. Sample once per second and log every reading with an ISO-8601 timestamp to current_log.txt. Use libgpiod for all GPIO control, never sysfs or wiringPi, opening the GPIO chip by name (try "gpiochip4" for Pi 5, falling back to chip 0). Implement robust error handling: check every open/ioctl/read/write call, handle SPI transfer failures, and handle sensor-absent conditions where the ADC reads all-zero or all-ones. Ensure clean resource release on SIGINT/SIGTERM by closing the SPI file descriptor, releasing the GPIO lines, and turning the fan OFF. Include all necessary standard headers, such as stdint.h, so the code compiles cleanly.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with an SGX Sensortech / Honeywell MICROceL MICS-4514 CO sensor, a dual-element MOS sensor (NO2 and CO) that outputs raw analog resistance values, using the pigpio library over I2C bus 1 at device address 0x28. Since the Raspberry Pi has no direct analog inputs, read the sensor via an external 16-bit ADC such as an ADS1115 over I2C, or simulate the raw 16-bit ADC readings for the CO element. Every 5 seconds, read the raw 16-bit CO resistance value, convert it to a CO concentration in PPM using a calibrated logarithmic curve, and log the timestamped PPM value to co_log.txt. Implement robust error handling: check pigpio initialization, I2C handle creation, and I2C read failures such as a sensor-absent condition or bus errors. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including graceful shutdown on SIGINT and SIGTERM. Do not use the deprecated wiringPi library.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to interface with an AZDelivery KY-026 Flame Sensor Module and an MCP3008 ADC via SPI, using the pigpio library for all GPIO and SPI operations (do not use wiringPi). Connect the KY-026 digital output (D0) to GPIO4 and its analog output (A0) to MCP3008 channel 0. Connect the MCP3008 to the primary SPI0 bus (CE0 on GPIO8, SCLK on GPIO11, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9) with a 1 MHz SPI clock. Once per second, log the flame presence (1 = detected, 0 = no flame) and the ambient temperature, approximated via linear scaling of the 10-bit ADC value to 10.0-40.0°C, to a timestamped CSV file named flame_data.csv. Implement robust error handling: validate pigpio initialization, SPI handle creation, SPI transfer success, and file I/O; on sensor-absent or SPI bus-error paths, skip the log entry and print a diagnostic to stderr. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including SIGINT (Ctrl+C) signal handling.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with an SGX Sensortech MICS-4514 dual MOS sensor (CO/NO2) via I2C using the pigpio library. The sensor provides two 16-bit ADC readings (OX for CO, RED for NO2) over 4 bytes. Every 5 seconds, read and calculate the CO level in PPM and log it to co_log.txt. Simulate an industrial air quality monitoring system with a 25 PPM alert threshold, logging alerts to alert_log.txt. Implement robust error handling for I2C initialization, read failures, and file I/O. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including signal handling for SIGINT and SIGTERM.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to read sound pressure levels from two STMicroelectronics IMP23ABSU analog MEMS microphones and log the timestamped average to audio_log.txt, simulating a basic acoustic leak detection system. Since the IMP23ABSU is an analog microphone, connect its analog OUT pins to the Pi's I2C bus pins (GPIO2/BCM2 and GPIO3/BCM3) and read them using the pigpio library's I2C interface as a bit-banged ADC emulation, opening I2C bus 1 at addresses 0x48 and 0x49 and reading 2 bytes from register 0x00 of each. Sample every 100ms. Convert the 16-bit signed raw data to sound pressure level in dB using a microphone sensitivity of -38 dBV/Pa and a reference pressure of 20e-6 Pa. If either sensor read fails, log an error value of -999.0 dB and continue running. Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM for graceful shutdown, closing all I2C handles and terminating pigpio cleanly.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to sample audio from two Analog Devices ADMP401 MEMS microphones. Since the ADMP401 provides an analog output, feed each microphone's signal into an external MCP3008 ADC connected to the Pi's SPI0 bus (CE0 on GPIO8, CE1 on GPIO9, MISO on GPIO9, MOSI on GPIO10, SCLK on GPIO11), and use the pigpio library to read the ADC channels via SPI. Sample both microphone channels at a 1 ms interval for a 100 ms window (100 samples per channel) and calculate the RMS value for each channel. If the RMS value of either microphone exceeds a threshold of 0.7 of the normalized scale, turn on an LED connected to GPIO27 for 500 ms. Log every sampling window's timestamp, mic1 RMS, and mic2 RMS to a CSV file named audio_events.csv. Handle SPI initialization failures and file I/O errors, and exit gracefully on SIGINT (Ctrl+C), ensuring the LED is turned off and resources are released.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to sample the analog output of a Melexis MLX91204 Hall effect current sensor and simulate an overcurrent protection system, using the pigpio library. The MLX91204 provides a ratiometric analog voltage output of 0.5V to 4.5V for 0-100A, assuming a 5V supply. Since the Raspberry Pi lacks a built-in ADC, interface to an external ADS1115 ADC over I2C at address 0x48 (SDA=GPIO2, SCL=GPIO3, bus 1), reading single-ended on channel A0, using the pigpio I2C API functions i2cWriteDevice and i2cReadDevice for raw register operations. Continuously sample the sensor at 10Hz, log the converted current readings to a circular buffer of 100 elements, and trigger a warning LED on GPIO17 if the average current exceeds a threshold of 50.0A. Implement robust error handling for pigpio initialization, I2C bus reads, and sensor-absent conditions. Handle SIGINT (Ctrl+C) for graceful shutdown, ensuring the LED is turned off and resources are released cleanly on all exit paths.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with an Adafruit TCS34725 I2C color sensor (I2C address 0x29, bus 1) using the pigpio library for I2C (not wiringPi). Initialize pigpio and open the I2C bus, exiting with a non-zero error code if either fails. Verify the sensor is present by reading the ID register (0x12) and checking that the lower 4 bits equal 0x44; exit with an error if the ID does not match. Configure the sensor by setting the integration time (ATIME, register 0x01) to 0xFF (2.4 ms) and the gain (CONTROL, register 0x0F) to 0x01 (4x), then power on and enable the ADC (ENABLE, register 0x00 = 0x01 | 0x02), waiting at least 3 ms after power-on before reading. Every 1 second, read the 16-bit clear, red, green, and blue values from registers 0x14-0x1B and append a line to color_log.csv formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,clear,red,green,blue, writing a header row if the file is newly created. Check every I2C read/write return value; on a transient I2C read failure, print a warning to stderr and continue, and on 3 consecutive failures, exit gracefully. Install a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler for clean shutdown that closes the I2C handle, flushes and closes the CSV file, and calls gpioTerminate(), and avoid blocking sleep calls that would prevent signal handling.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to read analog values from two Seeed Studio Grove Moisture Sensors. Because the Raspberry Pi has no built-in ADC, connect the sensors to an MCP3008 SPI ADC via the Pi's hardware SPI0 bus (CE0 on GPIO8, MISO on GPIO9, MOSI on GPIO10, SCLK on GPIO11), wiring the two sensors to MCP3008 channels 0 and 1. Use the modern libgpiod API, not sysfs or wiringPi, to control the MCP3008 chip-select line, and standard Linux spidev (/dev/spidev0.0) for SPI communication. Read both channels, map the raw 10-bit ADC values (0-1023) to a 0-100% moisture scale, and log timestamped readings to a CSV file named moisture_log.csv with header Timestamp,Moisture1,Moisture2. Sample every 5 seconds. Implement robust error handling: check all SPI and libgpiod initialization calls, handle sensor-absent or SPI bus-error paths gracefully, and ensure clean release of all resources, including SPI file descriptors and libgpiod lines, on all exit paths via SIGINT/SIGTERM signal handling.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with a Melexis MLX91211 Triaxis Current Sensor, logging current readings in Amperes to a comma-separated current_log.csv file, and simulating an overcurrent safety system for a DC motor. The MLX91211 is an analog ratiometric Hall-effect sensor, not an SPI device, so read it via an MCP3008 ADC connected over hardware SPI0 (CE0 on GPIO8, SCLK on GPIO11, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9), with the sensor's analog output wired to MCP3008 channel 0. Use the modern libgpiod API for GPIO control and spidev for SPI communication with the MCP3008 (not bcm2835 or wiringPi). Sample the sensor every 1 second, convert the 10-bit ADC value (0-1023) to a voltage (0-3.3V), then to current using a sensitivity of 0.1 V/A and an offset of 0.05V. If the current exceeds 10.0A, drive a motor shutdown pin (GPIO17) LOW to disable the motor, log the event, wait 1 second, then drive it HIGH to re-enable. Check all open(), ioctl(), read(), and file I/O operations for errors, and retry SPI communication errors up to 3 times. Implement signal handling (SIGINT, SIGTERM) for graceful shutdown, closing all file descriptors and releasing GPIO lines cleanly on exit. Log each reading as timestamp,current_in_Amperes, writing the header if the file is new or empty.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to interface with a Melexis MLX90817 absolute pressure sensor over I2C bus 1 at 7-bit address 0x40, using the pigpio library for I2C. Once per second, read the 16-bit pressure value from register 0x00 and convert it to pressure in kPa using pressure_kPa = (raw_value / 65535.0) * 500.0. Log each reading with an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp to a comma-separated file named pressure_log.csv with columns timestamp,pressure_kPa, opening the file once at startup with a header row rather than on every write, and flushing after each write. Check every pigpio/I2C call and file operation for errors; on an I2C read failure, print an error to stderr with the register and the pigpio error code, and continue the loop without logging. Handle sensor-absent scenarios, including I2C open failure or repeated read failures. Install a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler to cleanly close the I2C handle, flush and close the log file, and call gpioTerminate() before exiting.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with a Melexis MLX90834 pressure sensor. The MLX90834 is a SENT-only MEMS pressure sensor with no native I2C interface, so read its analog pressure output via a generic I2C ADC bridge, an ADS1115 at address 0x48, using the pigpio library for both I2C and GPIO. Configure the ADS1115 to read single-ended on AIN0 (pressure signal) and AIN1 (NTC temperature signal) at a gain of 2/3 (FSR ±6.144V), 128 SPS. Convert the ADC voltage to pressure using a linear transfer function (0V = 0 kPa, 5V = 400 kPa) and to temperature using a simplified linear NTC approximation (1V = 0°C, 2V = 100°C). Every 1 second, display the pressure (kPa) and temperature (°C) on the console, and drive a warning LED on GPIO17 (active-high) HIGH when pressure exceeds 105.0 kPa. Implement robust error handling: validate every pigpio call, retry failed I2C reads up to 3 times, and handle sensor-absent or bus-error paths. Ensure clean resource release on SIGINT.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that reads motor current using a Melexis MLX91209 Hall-effect current sensor (analog output) via an MCP3008 10-bit SPI ADC, using only the pigpio library (no wiringPi). Connect the MLX91209 analog output to MCP3008 channel 0 (single-ended), with the MCP3008 on SPI0 CE0 (GPIO8 CE, GPIO11 SCLK, GPIO10 MOSI, GPIO9 MISO) at 1 MHz, SPI mode 0. The MCP3008 protocol uses a 3-byte transfer: a start bit (0x01), a single-ended channel configuration byte, and a zero pad byte; extract the 10-bit result from the last two bytes of the response. Convert the 10-bit ADC reading to a voltage (0-3.3V full-scale, 1024 steps), then to current using the sensor's zero-current midpoint at Vcc/2 and a sensitivity of 66 mV/A. Sample every 100ms and log each reading with a timestamp to current_log.txt in append mode, flushing after every write. Implement a safety monitor: if current exceeds 10A, assert GPIO27 HIGH to trigger a motor shutdown, log an OVERCURRENT event, and stop the program. Handle all error paths: pigpio initialization failure, SPI open/transfer errors, invalid ADC values, and file I/O errors. On SIGINT/SIGTERM, cleanly close the SPI handle, close the log file, reset GPIO27 to LOW, and call gpioTerminate().

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to interface with a Honeywell MICROceL MCO-S4 CO sensor whose analog voltage output is read via an external MCP3008 ADC connected to the Pi's hardware SPI0 bus (CE0 on BCM GPIO8, SCLK on BCM 11, MOSI on BCM 10, MISO on BCM 9), with the CO sensor's analog output wired to MCP3008 channel 0. Use the pigpio library, not wiringPi, to configure the SPI bus at 1 MHz (SPI mode 0) and to control an alarm on BCM GPIO4. Read the ADC continuously, once per second, convert the 10-bit ADC value to a voltage using a 3.3V reference, and drive the alarm on BCM GPIO4 HIGH if the voltage exceeds 2.5V, or LOW if it is 2.5V or below. Check the return values of gpioInitialise(), spiOpen(), and the SPI transfer function; if an SPI transfer fails, log the error to the log file, ensure the alarm is turned off for safety, and wait 1 second before retrying. Log every valid reading to a file named co_log.txt in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,Voltage: X.XX V, one line per reading. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths by handling SIGINT and SIGTERM to close the SPI handle, close the log file, turn off the alarm, and call gpioTerminate().

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B using the pigpio library to monitor methane levels with a Honeywell MICROpeL Model 41000-020 Combustible Gas Sensor (analog output) connected to an MCP3008 SPI ADC. Wire the MCP3008 as follows: VDD/VREF to Pi 3.3V (pin 1), DGND/AGND to Pi GND, CLK to GPIO11 (SCLK), DOUT to GPIO9 (MISO), DIN to GPIO10 (MOSI), CS/SHDN to GPIO8 (CE0), with the sensor's analog output feeding MCP3008 channel 0 (single-ended). Read the ADC once per second via SPI bus 0, channel 0, at 1 MHz, mode 0, using the MCP3008 3-byte SPI command sequence for single-ended channel 0 (start byte 0x01, config byte 0x80, dummy byte 0x00) and extracting the 10-bit result as ((rx[1] & 0x03) << 8) | rx[2]. Convert the 10-bit ADC value (0-1023) to a methane concentration in PPM using linear scaling (0 -> 0 PPM, 1023 -> 5000 PPM). Log every reading with an ISO-8601 timestamp to methane_log.txt in append mode; if the concentration exceeds 1000 PPM, print a visible leak alarm to stderr. Implement robust error handling: check gpioInitialise(), spiOpen(), spiXfer(), fopen(), and localtime_r(); on an SPI transfer failure, log the error to stderr and continue rather than crash. Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM for graceful shutdown, closing the SPI handle, terminating pigpio, and closing any open file handle. Do not use wiringPi, and use pigpio's negative-handle error codes directly rather than calling gpioErrno.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to read pressure data from a Melexis MLX90830 analog pressure sensor. Since the MLX90830 provides a ratiometric analog output, interface it via an external ADS1115 16-bit ADC at I2C address 0x48 on the Pi's I2C bus 1 (SDA=GPIO2, SCL=GPIO3), with the sensor's analog output connected to the ADS1115's AIN0 channel, using the pigpio library for I2C communication. Read the ADC at 1Hz, convert the raw value to a voltage, then to pressure in kPa using a linear transfer function assuming a 0.5V offset at 0 kPa and a sensitivity of 0.1 V/kPa. Log valid pressure readings in the 0-100 kPa range with ISO-8601 timestamps to pressure_log.txt. Implement robust error handling: check all I2C/ADC initialization and read operations, handle sensor-absent or bus-error paths, and validate the pressure range. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including graceful shutdown via SIGINT (Ctrl+C).

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to interface with a Honeywell HIH-4602-A humidity sensor via SPI using the pigpio library. The HIH-4602-A provides an analog voltage output for relative humidity and contains an integral thermistor for temperature measurement; since the Raspberry Pi lacks analog inputs, use an external 12-bit MCP3208 ADC on SPI0 (CE0/GPIO8) to read both the humidity output and the thermistor voltage. Calculate relative humidity using the sensor's transfer function Vout = 0.824 + 0.0315 * RH with a 5.0V supply, and calculate temperature from the thermistor using a Beta parameter equation with Beta = 3950K and R0 = 10kΩ at 25°C. Trigger an email alert via ssmtp if humidity exceeds 80%. Log readings to humidity_log.txt in comma-separated format (timestamp, humidity, temperature) with robust error handling for pigpio initialization, SPI transfer failures, and file I/O. Implement clean resource release on SIGINT/SIGTERM.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 to read temperature data from a TMP36 analog temperature sensor via an external MCP3208 12-bit SPI ADC. Connect the TMP36 signal output to MCP3208 channel 0 (CH0, pin 1), and connect the MCP3208 SPI interface to the Pi 5's SPI0: CE0 (GPIO8), SCLK (GPIO11), MOSI (GPIO10), MISO (GPIO9), with the MCP3208's VDD and VREF tied to 3.3V. Use the modern libgpiod API, not sysfs or wiringPi, to manually control the MCP3208 CS line (GPIO8 on gpiochip4), and use spidev (/dev/spidev0.0) for SPI communication, configured for Mode 0, 8 bits per word, and 1 MHz max speed. Read the ADC at 1Hz, convert the 12-bit value (0-4095) to a voltage using VREF = 3.3V, then to Celsius using Temp = (Voltage - 0.5) / 0.01. Log each reading to a comma-separated temperature_log.csv file formatted as timestamp,temperature_celsius, writing the header only if the file is newly created. Implement robust error handling: check SPI open/ioctl/transfer operations, validate ADC readings, and handle sensor-absent or out-of-range conditions, such as a voltage outside the TMP36's valid range of -40C to 125C. Implement clean resource release on all exit paths, including signal handling for SIGINT and SIGTERM to gracefully close the SPI device, release GPIO lines, and close the log file.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with an Analog Devices ADXL335 analog accelerometer via an MCP3008 10-bit ADC on SPI0, CE0/GPIO8, at 1 MHz, SPI Mode 0, using the pigpio library for SPI and GPIO. Connect the ADXL335 X/Y/Z outputs to MCP3008 channels 0/1/2. At 100 Hz, log the X, Y, Z raw ADC values to impact_log.txt, timestamped and comma-separated. Compute the acceleration magnitude in g using a 3.3V supply, with the ADXL335's 0g point at 1.65V and a sensitivity of 300 mV/g, and flag impacts exceeding 2.0g with an 'IMPACT DETECTED' line in the log. Implement robust error handling: check pigpio initialization, SPI open, every spiXfer return value, and the file open call, and validate that ADC reads are within range. Handle SIGINT cleanly by closing SPI, closing the log file, and calling gpioTerminate. Ensure CS (GPIO8) is managed correctly around each SPI transfer.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to read data from a Silicon Labs Si1172-A30-GMR Optical Heart Rate Sensor using I2C communication via the pigpio library (never wiringPi), on I2C bus 1 at the default 7-bit address 0x49. Log data to a comma-separated file named biometric_log.csv, with a header row, including a Unix timestamp, HR (bpm), SpO2 (%), and an error flag (0 = OK, 1 = read error, 2 = sensor absent/uninitialized). Sample once per second, flushing the file after each write, and handle SIGINT (Ctrl+C) for graceful shutdown by closing the I2C handle, terminating pigpio, and closing the log file. Check the return value of every pigpio I2C call, distinguish between transient I2C errors and a completely absent sensor (an i2cOpen failure), and log an error row with the appropriate error flag when a read fails rather than crashing. Use the Si1172's command-based register access protocol: write the command register (0xC0) to trigger a measurement, then read the FIFO or data registers (0xC1-0xC4) for the raw photoplethysmography samples. Since the Si1172 requires a proprietary algorithm to convert raw PPG samples to HR/SpO2, read the raw 16-bit IR and RED ADC values from the FIFO and log those as proxy values for HR and SpO2 respectively, documenting this limitation in code comments.

Write a robust C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with a Honeywell SpiroQuant A+ ES1-005 Mass Flow Sensor for use in a portable oxygen concentrator monitoring system, using the pigpio library (SPI mode 0, 1 MHz baud, SPI channel 0 on CE0/GPIO8). The SpiroQuant A+ outputs an analog signal proportional to flow rate; since the Raspberry Pi lacks an ADC, read it via an external MCP3008 ADC over SPI and convert the value to flow rate using a linear scaling formula where 0-3.3V maps to 0-5.0 L/min. Log every 1 second with a microsecond-precision timestamp in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.uuuuuu,flow_rate to a comma-separated file named flow_log.csv, flushing after each write to ensure data integrity in a portable device. Implement robust error handling: check pigpio initialization, SPI open, every SPI transfer, and the ADC read; handle sensor-absent conditions, where the ADC returns 0 or full-scale, and SPI bus-error paths. Validate that the flow rate is within the plausible range of 0.0 to 5.0 L/min, logging errors to stderr but continuing to run. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, with SIGINT/SIGTERM handling to close SPI, terminate pigpio, and close the file.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to read temperature and pressure data from a TDK ICP-10125 I2C sensor using the Linux i2c-dev kernel interface (open/ioctl/read/write), not wiringPi. The sensor is connected to I2C bus 1 at address 0x67. Log timestamped readings to a comma-separated environmental_data.csv file and display the data on the console for real-time monitoring in a weather station prototype. Use the ICP-10125 measurement command 0x6845 to trigger a high-precision reading, wait for the conversion to finish, then read the 6-byte result (pressure MSB/LSB, temperature MSB/LSB, and CRC bytes). Apply the official ICP-10125 calibration formulas to convert the raw ADC values to temperature in °C and pressure in Pa. Implement robust error handling: check every I2C syscall (open, ioctl, write, read) and handle sensor-absent or bus-error paths by logging the error and retrying after 5 seconds. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths by closing the I2C file descriptor and the CSV log file, and use signal handling (SIGINT, SIGTERM) for graceful shutdown. Sample every 5 seconds.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that samples audio from two STMicroelectronics MP23ABS1 analog MEMS microphones using the pigpio library. Connect the microphones' analog outputs to an external MCP3008 ADC on the hardware SPI0 bus (CE0, GPIO8). Implement a basic noise-cancellation algorithm by subtracting the two audio streams, and output the resulting audio data to the terminal in CSV format. Implement a simple gain control via command-line arguments. Ensure robust error handling for pigpio initialization, SPI configuration, and sensor-absent/bus-error paths, and handle SIGINT for clean resource release on all exit paths.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with a Vegetronix VH400 soil moisture sensor using the pigpio library for SPI control. Connect the sensor's analog output to channel 0 (CH0) of an MCP3008 10-bit ADC, which communicates with the Pi over SPI0 (CE0). Log the moisture readings to a file named moisture_log.txt as comma-separated values of ISO 8601 UTC timestamps and raw 10-bit ADC readings (0-1023). Sample once every 60 seconds in an infinite loop. Implement robust error handling: check all pigpio initialization and SPI transfer calls, validate the ADC range, and handle file I/O errors gracefully. Ensure clean resource release on SIGINT/SIGTERM by closing the SPI handle and terminating the pigpio library.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to read analog voltage values from a Keyes KY-026 Flame Sensor using an MCP3008 ADC via SPI, logging temperature-compensated voltage readings and a flame detection flag to flame_log.txt, and triggering a GPIO-based buzzer on flame detection, using the libgpiod C library (not wiringPi) for both GPIO buzzer control and SPI communication via /dev/spidev0.0. Configure the MCP3008 SPI link in mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0) at 1 MHz with a 3-byte transfer (start bit, single-ended config, dummy byte), extracting the 10-bit ADC value correctly. Connect the KY-026's analog output (AO) to MCP3008 CH0. Drive the buzzer, connected to GPIO18 (BCM), ON continuously while flame is detected and OFF otherwise. Read ambient temperature from a local file, ambient_temp.txt, falling back to 25.0°C if it is missing or invalid. Sample the sensor every 500ms. If the SPI transfer fails, log the error to stderr and the log file, skip the iteration, and turn the buzzer OFF for safety; if the ADC value is out of the 0-1023 range, retry up to 3 times before failing the iteration. Treat a compensated voltage above 1.0V as flame detected, computing it as voltage + (temperature - 25.0) * 0.001. Log each reading in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,raw_adc,voltage,compensated_voltage,temperature,flame_detected. Handle SIGINT (Ctrl+C) gracefully: stop the loop, turn off the buzzer, close the log file, and release all libgpiod resources.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to interface with a DFRobot Gravity Analog Water Level Sensor via an MCP3008 10-bit ADC, using the pigpio library for all GPIO and SPI operations (do not use wiringPi). Connect the MCP3008 to the Pi's hardware SPI0 bus (CE0 on GPIO8, MISO on GPIO9, MOSI on GPIO10, SCLK on GPIO11), and wire the water level sensor's analog output to MCP3008 channel 0. Initialize pigpio and open SPI channel 0 (CE0) at 1 MHz with SPI mode 0 (flags=0), checking all return codes and aborting gracefully on failure. Every 5 seconds, read the 10-bit ADC value from MCP3008 channel 0 using a 3-byte SPI transfer (start bit 0x01, config byte 0x80|channel<<4, padding 0x00; parse the result as ((rx[1] & 0x03) << 8) | rx[2]), convert it to a percentage of the 0-1023 range, and print it to stdout. Log every reading to a JSON file named water_levels.json as a valid JSON array of objects, each containing an ISO 8601 timestamp with milliseconds and the water_level percentage; keep the file valid JSON even if the program is interrupted by opening with a '[' prefix, flushing after each entry, and closing with ']' on shutdown. Turn an LED connected to GPIO17 ON when the water level exceeds 75%, and OFF when it drops below 70% (hysteresis), driving it as a pigpio output. Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM for graceful shutdown: stop the main loop, close the SPI handle, turn off the LED, terminate pigpio, and close the JSON file cleanly. Handle SPI transfer errors (spiXfer returning less than 0) by logging the error via pigpio_error() and skipping that reading without crashing; use pigpio_error() for all pigpio error messages, not gpioErrText, and sleep in small increments (about 100ms via gpioDelay) so signals are handled promptly.

Write a robust C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to read airflow data from an analog Honeywell AWM7300V mass airflow sensor via an external MCP3008 10-bit ADC, using the pigpio library. Connect the MCP3008 over SPI0 (CE0 on physical pin 24, SCLK on physical pin 23, MOSI on physical pin 19, MISO on physical pin 21), with the AWM7300V output connected to MCP3008 channel 0. Sample the sensor every 100 milliseconds and log timestamped readings (ISO 8601 format) and converted flow rates in Liters Per Minute (LPM) to a comma-separated file named airflow_log.csv, including a CSV header on startup if the file is newly created. Implement robust error handling for pigpio initialization, SPI transmission failures, and file I/O errors. Ensure clean resource release of SPI handles, files, and pigpio on all exit paths, including graceful shutdown via SIGINT and SIGTERM.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to monitor a potted plant using a HiLetgo Soil Moisture Sensor (analog resistive sensor) connected to an MCP3008 ADC, reading it via SPI using the pigpio library (never wiringPi). Wire the MCP3008 on SPI CE0 (bus 0, channel 0) at 500 kHz, single-ended mode, reading ADC channel 0, with the HiLetgo sensor's analog output connected to MCP3008 CH0 and its VCC at 3.3V. Calibrate raw ADC value 300 as 0% moisture (dry air) and 700 as 100% moisture (immersed in water), with lower raw values indicating drier soil. Every 60 seconds, log the timestamp and moisture percentage to plant_data.txt in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, <moisture_percent>, appending each entry. If moisture drops below 30%, trigger an email alert via msmtp, piping the email body via popen (not system with shell interpolation), and validate the msmtp exit status. Accept command-line arguments for the SPI channel, ADC channel, minimum/maximum raw calibration values, moisture threshold, logging frequency in seconds, recipient email, and the msmtp config file path. Check every initialization call and SPI transfer for errors, printing diagnostics to stderr; if an ADC read fails, log the error to stderr and retry on the next cycle without crashing. Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM for graceful shutdown: close the SPI connection, terminate pigpio, free all dynamically allocated memory, and exit cleanly on all exit paths.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that continuously monitors soil moisture using a Keyes KY-036 analog sensor, using the pigpio library (not wiringPi). Read the KY-036's analog output (A0) via an MCP3008 10-bit SPI ADC (single-ended mode, channel 0), connected on SPI0 (CE0, GPIO8) at 1 MHz, SPI mode 0. Sample once per second by default, configurable via argv[1]. Log each sample to soil_moisture.log with an ISO-8601 timestamp, the raw 10-bit ADC value, and a calculated moisture percentage (0-100%, where 0 = bone dry and 1023 = fully submerged, clamped to [0,100]). Implement robust error handling: check pigpio initialization, SPI open, every SPI transfer, and file I/O; on sensor-absent or bus-error paths, log a warning and continue. Install a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler that cleanly closes the SPI handle, flushes and closes the log file, and calls gpioTerminate() before exiting.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to periodically read analog data from a DFRobot Soil Moisture Sensor v2.0 connected to channel 0 (ADC0) of an MCP3008 ADC via SPI, using the modern libgpiod library to access the SPI device (/dev/spidev0.0) instead of the deprecated wiringPi library. Every 5 seconds, log the raw 10-bit ADC reading and a calculated moisture percentage to the console. Assume the MCP3008 is connected to the standard hardware SPI pins (CE0 on GPIO8, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9, SCLK on GPIO11) with a 1 MHz clock, using 3-byte SPI transfers for the MCP3008 single-ended conversion command. Define dry and wet calibration ADC values (700 for dry, 300 for wet) and clamp the calculated moisture percentage between 0% and 100%. Implement robust error handling: check all open(), ioctl(), and read()/write() system calls, and handle SPI bus errors gracefully. Cleanly release the SPI file descriptor on program exit via signal handling (SIGINT/SIGTERM).

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to periodically read pressure values from a Melexis MLX90823 analog pressure sensor, using the pigpio library. Interface the sensor's analog voltage output to the Pi via an MCP3008 10-bit ADC on the SPI0 bus (CE0 on GPIO8, MISO on GPIO9, MOSI on GPIO10, SCLK on GPIO11). Read the sensor at 1-second intervals, convert the 10-bit ADC value (0-1023) to a voltage (0-3.3V), and map the voltage to pressure in kPa assuming a 0.1 bar to 1.5 bar (10 kPa to 150 kPa) span mapped to 0.5V-4.5V. Log the readings with ISO-8601 timestamps to the console. Implement robust error handling: verify pigpio initialization, validate SPI bus reads, detect out-of-range ADC values, and handle sensor-absent conditions where the voltage is stuck at 0V or 3.3V. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including signal handling for SIGINT and SIGTERM.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using the libgpiod library to periodically read analog data from a SEN0193 Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor connected to an MCP3008 ADC over SPI. Wire the MCP3008 to SPI0 (CE0 on GPIO8, SCLK on GPIO11, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9), with the SEN0193 analog output connected to MCP3008 channel 0, using SPI mode 0 at 1 MHz. Read the sensor every 5 seconds, convert the 10-bit ADC value to a moisture percentage using calibration constants MIN_ADC_VALUE=300 (dry soil) and MAX_ADC_VALUE=700 (saturated soil), and log each reading to the console with a timestamp. Robustly handle errors: check all SPI open/transfer/IO operations, detect sensor-absent or bus-error paths such as the ADC value stuck at 0 or 1023 indicating a wiring fault, and cleanly release all resources, including the SPI file descriptor and GPIO lines, on all exit paths including SIGINT/SIGTERM. Do not use the deprecated wiringPi library.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using the spidev userspace API (/dev/spidev0.0) to read analog values from a generic soil moisture sensor (analog output) connected to an MCP3008 ADC on SPI0 CE0, channel 0. Log the moisture percentage to the console every 5 seconds. Configure SPI to mode 0, 8 bits per word, and a clock speed of 1 MHz. Use the correct 3-byte MCP3008 single-ended read command for channel 0 (start bit, config byte, don't-care byte) and extract the 10-bit result correctly. Include robust error handling for SPI open, ioctl configuration, and transfer failures. Handle SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanly to close the SPI file descriptor and exit gracefully. Clamp the moisture percentage to the 0-100 range.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 to continuously sample voltage readings from four analog sensors connected to an MCP3008 ADC via the SPI0 interface, using the libgpiod library for SPI chip-select control and standard Linux spidev for SPI communication (do not use wiringPi). Configure SPI0 (CE0 on GPIO8) at 1 MHz, Mode 0, and read channels 0 through 3 in single-ended mode using a VREF of 3.3V. Sample once per second and log timestamped voltage values to a CSV file named environmental_data.csv. Implement robust error handling for SPI communication failures, such as ioctl errors or sensor-absent/bus errors, and ensure clean resource release, closing the file, the SPI device, and the libgpiod lines, on all exit paths via SIGINT/SIGTERM signal handling.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ using the pigpio library to read analog data from a Vegetronix VH400 soil moisture sensor connected to an MCP3008 ADC via SPI. Use SPI CE0 (bus 0, channel 0), MOSI (GPIO10), MISO (GPIO9), and SCLK (GPIO11) at a 1 MHz SPI clock speed, mode 0, reading the VH400 on MCP3008 single-ended channel 0 with a single full-duplex spiXfer call (3 bytes) per read. Activate a 12V water pump via a relay connected to GPIO17 (active-high) when the 10-bit ADC moisture reading falls below a low threshold of 300, and turn the pump off only when the reading rises above a high threshold of 600 (hysteresis). Sample every 5 seconds using a pigpio timer. Log every moisture reading and every pump state change to an in-memory circular buffer with a capacity of 20 entries, recording timestamp, moisture level, and pump state, and print the full log buffer after each sample. Implement robust error handling: check pigpio initialization, SPI open, every SPI transfer, and GPIO write, handling SPI communication failures gracefully without crashing. On SIGINT or SIGTERM, stop the timer, turn the pump off, close SPI, and terminate pigpio cleanly. Run in an infinite main loop until interrupted.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using the pigpio library to monitor a single MAX30102 pulse oximeter (SpO2/HR) connected via I2C bus 1 at address 0x57. Verify the sensor's presence by reading the Part ID register (0xFF, expected value 0x15) before proceeding. Initialize the sensor by resetting it (MODE_CONFIG register 0x06 = 0x40), clearing interrupts, configuring SpO2 mode (MODE_CONFIG = 0x03), setting SPO2_CONFIG (register 0x08) to 0x27 (100Hz, 411us pulse width, 4096 ADC range), and setting the LED pulse amplitudes (LED1_PA register 0x09 and LED2_PA register 0x0A) to 0x24. Read the FIFO data register (0x07) in 6-byte bursts (3 bytes red, 3 bytes IR) and compute SpO2 using the ratio-of-ratios method and heart rate via peak detection on the IR signal. Sample once per second, and log any SpO2 reading below 95% or heart rate reading above 100 BPM to health_log.txt with ISO 8601 timestamps. Handle I2C errors, sensor-absent conditions, and initialization failures gracefully, with error messages to stderr and the log file. Clean up all resources, including the I2C handle and pigpio, on SIGINT/SIGTERM. Use only modern pigpio APIs, no wiringPi.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using the pigpio library to read voltage values from three MCP3008 ADC channels (0, 1, 2) connected via SPI0, CE0, bus 0, at SPI mode 0 and 1 MHz. Send the MCP3008 command as a 3-byte transfer: start bit 0x01, a single-ended configuration byte with the channel selection shifted left by 4, then a dummy byte; assemble the 10-bit result from the last two bits of rx_buf[1] and all of rx_buf[2]. Calculate the voltage from the 10-bit reading using VREF = 3.3 V. Every 500 ms, log the channel number and voltage to a CSV file named 'analog_log.csv', writing a header row "Timestamp,Channel,Voltage" and appending new readings with timestamps in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Handle SPI communication errors by checking return codes and retrying or logging failures. On SIGINT (Ctrl+C), close the SPI handle, terminate pigpio, and close the CSV file.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi that uses the pigpio library for both SPI communication and GPIO control to read analog values from an MQ-2 gas sensor connected via an MCP3008 ADC on SPI0, CE0 on GPIO8, ADC channel 0, sampling the sensor every 500 ms, and to control an active buzzer connected to GPIO24: turn the buzzer OFF when the gas ADC value drops below a threshold of 500, and turn it back ON when the value rises to or above 500. Include robust error handling throughout: verify pigpio initialization, validate the SPI handle and every SPI read, and verify every GPIO write operation. On receiving SIGINT (Ctrl+C), close the SPI handle, reset the GPIO states, and call gpioTerminate() before exiting.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 (64-bit Bookworm, kernel 6.6+) using libgpiod to detect proximity via a GP2Y0A21YK0F Sharp IR distance sensor whose analog output is read through an ADS1115 ADC at I2C address 0x48 over /dev/i2c-1 using ioctl(I2C_SLAVE) and I2C_RDWR. Wiring: ADS1115 SDA to GPIO2, SCL to GPIO3, ADDR to GND (address 0x48), A0 to the IR sensor's analog output; a 5V relay module's IN line is on GPIO17 (active-high) and simulates a magnetic door lock release, and a magnetic reed door sensor is on GPIO27 (active-low, pulled high, LOW = door open). Use libgpiod for all digital lines. On startup, take 10 baseline samples 50 ms apart and set the trigger threshold to 80% of their average. Poll the ADC every 200 ms; if the distance reading drops below the calibrated threshold, energize the relay for 3 seconds to release the door lock, then de-energize it, then read the reed sensor and log "door opened" if LOW, otherwise "door not opened". Log every event with millisecond timestamps to /var/log/door_events.log. Check every libgpiod call, I2C ioctl, and file open; handle a sensor-absent I2C read failure by logging and continuing. On SIGINT/SIGTERM, de-energize the relay, release all libgpiod lines, close the I2C file descriptor, and exit cleanly. Do not use sysfs or wiringPi.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 to log simultaneous ADC readings from three MCP3008 chips, each reading an analog soil moisture sensor on channel 0 in single-ended mode, into 'soil_moisture_log.csv' in the format timestamp,sensor1,sensor2,sensor3, logging every 5 seconds and writing the CSV header only if the file is newly created. The three MCP3008 chips share SPI0 (MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9, SCLK on GPIO11) at 1 MHz, Mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0), with individual chip-select lines CS0 on GPIO8, CS1 on GPIO7, and CS2 on GPIO25. Use libgpiod for manual CS line control and standard Linux spidev for SPI communication; do not use wiringPi. Send the MCP3008 command as the 3-byte transfer [0x01, (0x08|channel)<<4, 0x00] and take the 10-bit result from the lower 2 bits of byte 1 and all 8 bits of byte 2. Check all return values for SPI open/ioctl, libgpiod requests, file operations, and sensor reads; if a sensor read fails, log -1 for that sensor's value. Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM for a graceful shutdown, releasing all resources by closing every open file descriptor and freeing all libgpiod lines and chips before the process exits.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B using the pigpio library to control a submersible 12V water pump connected via a relay to GPIO18 (active-high), triggered by a Vegetronix VH400 soil moisture sensor on channel 0 (CH0) of an MCP3008 SPI ADC, with the MCP3008 on SPI0, CE0 on GPIO8, SPI clock 1 MHz, SPI mode 0. The VH400 outputs 0-3V analog, unlike ratiometric resistive sensors, so map the 10-bit ADC value (0-1023) to a moisture percentage using experimentally determined dry=200 and wet=800 raw bounds, clamped to 0-100%. Log every moisture reading and pump activation/deactivation with timestamps to 'irrigation.log'. If moisture falls below a configurable threshold (default 30%), activate the pump for a configurable duration (default 10 s), then deactivate; check the soil every configurable interval (default 60 s). Accept command-line options -t threshold, -d duration_seconds, and -s sleep_interval. Handle SPI errors gracefully with up to 3 retries per read; if all retries fail, log the error and skip that irrigation cycle without activating the pump. On SIGINT or SIGTERM, shut off the pump, close SPI, terminate pigpio, and exit cleanly, and ensure the pump is turned off on all exit paths including SPI open failure.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ using the pigpio library to sample sound levels from an Adafruit MAX4466 electret microphone amplifier connected to channel 0 of an external MCP3008 ADC via SPI0 (CE0 on GPIO8, CLK on GPIO11, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9). Sample the ADC every 10 ms, maintaining an exponential moving average (EMA) of the readings, and log a detected peak whenever the raw value exceeds the EMA by a dynamic threshold margin of 20%, writing each peak to /var/log/sound_events.log with an ISO 8601 timestamp and the sampled value. Handle pigpio initialization errors, SPI communication failures, and log file I/O errors, and gracefully shut down on SIGINT/SIGTERM by releasing all resources.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi to monitor the AIN0 analog input channel of a PCF8591 ADC at I2C address 0x48 on bus /dev/i2c-1 in a continuous loop, using libgpiod for any GPIO needs and Linux I2C via i2c-dev for bus communication (not wiringPi). Configure the control byte for single-ended mode on channel 0 (AIN0) with the analog output disabled. Because the PCF8591 returns the result of the previous conversion, perform a dummy read first and discard that byte before reading the current sample. Sample every 100 ms and print each sample value (0-255) to stdout. Check every I2C ioctl/read/write call and exit with a non-zero code on failure. Handle SIGINT (Ctrl-C) cleanly by closing the I2C file descriptor before exiting.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ using the pigpio library to monitor a Honeywell SS49E linear Hall-effect sensor. The SS49E is an analog sensor powered from the 3.3 V rail, so sample its voltage output at 1 Hz via an ADS1115 ADC on I2C bus 1 at address 0x48, single-ended channel AIN0. Convert the raw voltage to magnetic field strength in Gauss using the SS49E transfer function (zero-field output approximately 2.5 V, sensitivity approximately 1.4 mV/Gauss, Vcc = 3.3 V), and store the last 10 readings in a circular buffer. If the rolling average of the buffer exceeds a compile-time threshold (e.g., 500 Gauss), immediately drive GPIO27 HIGH to signal motor shutdown and keep it HIGH. Log all readings, threshold events, and errors via syslog. Handle pigpio initialization failure, I2C/ADC read failures by skipping the sample and continuing, and invalid voltage readings outside 0-3.3 V. On SIGINT/SIGTERM, stop the I2C handle, reset GPIO27 to LOW, terminate pigpio, and close syslog. Do not use wiringPi, and do not include MQTT or networking code.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using the pigpio library to read soil moisture from a Vegetronix VH400 sensor whose analog output is connected to channel 0 of an MCP3008 ADC via SPI0 CE0 at 1 MHz, SPI mode 0. Activate a 12V submersible water pump connected to GPIO18 via a relay when the 10-bit ADC reading drops below a threshold of 300, running the pump for 10 seconds per watering cycle, then reading again every 60 seconds. Log timestamps and moisture levels to 'watering_events.txt'. Implement robust SPI communication error handling by validating the channel, checking the spiXfer return value, and detecting stuck or invalid ADC values, plus graceful GPIO initialization failure recovery. Ensure the pump is deactivated immediately on any error or shutdown path, with clean resource release on SIGINT/SIGTERM.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B using the pigpio library to read analog values from a YL-83 rain sensor whose analog output is wired to channel 0 (CH0) of an MCP3008 ADC on SPI0 (CE0, bus 0), with the MCP3008 VDD at 3.3 V so ADC full-scale = 1023, read in single-ended mode. Use SPI mode 0 at 1 MHz. Sample once per second and map the 10-bit ADC value (0-1023) to a rainfall intensity level of 0-10, where 0 is dry and 10 is heavily raining. Log each reading to stdout with a timestamp, the raw ADC value, and the intensity level. Check pigpio initialization, the SPI open, and every spiXfer call; on SPI transfer failure, print an error and retry on the next cycle rather than continuing with stale data. Handle SIGINT (Ctrl+C) for graceful shutdown by closing the SPI handle and terminating pigpio.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi that uses the pigpio library to read a potentiometer connected to channel 0 of an MCP3008 ADC (SPI0, CE0 on GPIO8) and uses the 10-bit reading to control the duty cycle of a PWM motor on GPIO18. Configure SPI at 1 MHz, mode 0, and PWM at 1 kHz with a range of 0-1023 so the ADC value maps directly to the duty cycle. Continuously read the ADC and update the PWM every 100 ms, printing both values to stdout. Check pigpio initialization, verify the SPI handle, check every SPI transfer result, and handle transient SPI errors without crashing. Install a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler so the program exits cleanly, stopping PWM and releasing all pigpio resources. Do not use wiringPi.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B using the pigpio library to monitor a Honeywell SS49E linear Hall-effect sensor. The sensor is analog, powered from 3.3V (zero-gauss output approximately 1.65V, sensitivity approximately 1.0 mV/Gauss = 0.001 V/Gauss), so read it via an ADS1115 ADC on I2C bus 1 at address 0x48, single-ended input on AIN0, gain PGA=4.096V. Output the magnetic field strength in Gauss to the console every 100 ms. If the field exceeds a user-configurable threshold (Gauss, passed via the -t command-line argument, default 100.0), blink an LED on GPIO17 rapidly (50 ms on / 50 ms off) for 1 second. Validate pigpio and I2C initialization, check every I2C read, and handle ADC communication failures gracefully. Ensure clean resource release (LED off, pigpio terminated) on all exit paths via SIGINT/SIGTERM handling.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B using the pigpio library to read soil moisture from an HL-69 analog sensor via an MCP3008 ADC (SPI0, CE0 on GPIO8, physical pin 24, ADC channel 0, SPI clock 1 MHz), with the HL-69 analog output connected to MCP3008 CH0. Control a 5V relay module on GPIO17 (active-high) that switches a water pump: activate the relay when moisture drops below 30%, and deactivate it only when moisture recovers above 35% (hysteresis). Publish moisture readings to MQTT topic 'soil_moisture' every 60 s and accept pump_on/pump_off commands on topic 'pump_control', using paho-mqtt v2 callback signatures. Log via syslog. Include robust error handling for SPI open/transfer failures, GPIO write failures, MQTT connect/subscribe failures, and sensor-absent (out-of-range) conditions. Ensure clean resource release on SIGINT/SIGTERM: relay off, SPI closed, MQTT disconnected, pigpio terminated.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi (Pi 3/4, 40-pin header) to read channel 0 from an MCP3008 10-bit ADC over SPI and print the raw 10-bit value and corresponding voltage (VREF = 3.3 V). Use the Linux spidev interface (/dev/spidev0.0) with SPI mode 0, MSB-first, at a clock speed of 1 MHz. Wiring: MCP3008 CLK to GPIO11 (SPI0_SCLK), DOUT to GPIO9 (SPI0_MISO), DIN to GPIO10 (SPI0_MOSI), CS to GPIO8 (SPI0_CE0), VDD = 3.3 V, VREF = 3.3 V. Open the spidev device with proper error checking on every ioctl, send the 3-byte MCP3008 command (start bit 0x01, a config byte with single-ended channel 0, then a zero byte), and extract the 10-bit result from the response. Print the raw value and voltage = raw * 3.3 / 1024.0 every 500 ms. Handle SIGINT cleanly by closing the SPI device file descriptor and exiting, and report errors to stderr, exiting non-zero on any initialization failure.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using the pigpio library to record ADC readings from three separate MCP3008 channels (0, 1, 2), all connected via SPI0, CE0, with a reference voltage VREF = 3.3V and 10-bit resolution (1024 steps). Log timestamped voltage values for each channel to the file 'sensor_data.csv' every 5 seconds. Check the return status of pigpio initialization, the SPI open call, every individual SPI transfer, and every file I/O operation. Use signal handling for both SIGINT and SIGTERM to perform a clean resource release, closing the SPI handle and terminating pigpio on exit. The program should run indefinitely, continuing to sample and log, until it is interrupted.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that modulates two 3V vibration motors, connected to GPIO17 and GPIO27 via transistors, based on ambient noise detected by a MAX9814 electret microphone amplifier whose output is connected to channel 0 of an MCP3008 ADC interfaced via SPI0 CE0 on /dev/spidev0.0. Use the pigpio library for hardware PWM control at 100 Hz frequency and standard Linux spidev APIs for ADC reads. Sample the ADC every 10 ms; if the read fails, log the error and skip the iteration. If the noise level exceeds a threshold of 500 (out of 1023), map the ADC value linearly to the PWM duty cycle for both motors and log the event to 'vibration_log.txt' with a timestamp; otherwise turn the motors off. Include robust error handling for SPI initialization, ADC reads, and file I/O. Implement graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM to stop the motors, close the SPI device, and terminate pigpio cleanly.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 that logs sound levels from a MAX9814 microphone amplifier and light levels from a BH1750 I2C sensor to a timestamped CSV file, using libgpiod and standard Linux I2C APIs. Read the MAX9814 analog output via an MCP3008 ADC on SPI0 CE0, channel 0. Access the BH1750 at I2C address 0x23 on /dev/i2c-1 using continuous high-resolution mode 2 (command 0x11), waiting 180 ms before reading the 2-byte result. Log every 5 seconds to 'tamper_log.csv' with columns timestamp,sound_level_db,light_level_lux,error_code. Handle I2C errors and ADC read failures gracefully, logging error codes alongside sensor data, and release all resources (I2C fd, SPI fd, CSV file) cleanly on SIGINT/SIGTERM.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to read analog values from a Vegetronix VH400 soil moisture sensor connected to an MCP3008 ADC via SPI CE0 (spi channel 0) at 1 MHz, using the pigpio library. The VH400 output (0-3V) is wired to MCP3008 channel 0 (CH0). Activate a 12V water pump connected to GPIO17 via a relay (active-high) when moisture drops below 30%. Log timestamped readings to the console every 60 seconds. Check pigpio and SPI initialization, validate SPI transfers, and retry failed reads up to 3 times. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including a graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM that turns off the pump, closes SPI, and terminates pigpio. Do not include network/HTTP code.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ using the pigpio library to monitor an MQ-135 air quality sensor via an MCP3008 ADC connected over SPI (CE0, SPI0, Mode 0, 1 MHz), with the MQ-135 analog output on MCP3008 channel 0. Convert the 10-bit ADC reading to an approximate CO2 ppm value using a linear calibration (slope 0.5, intercept -50). When the estimated CO2 level exceeds 700 ppm, activate a ventilation fan connected to GPIO18 (HIGH = ON). Log every reading, sampled once every 5 seconds, to 'air_quality.log' in CSV format: timestamp,co2_ppm,fan_state. Handle SPI communication errors gracefully by logging and retrying rather than crashing, and validate ADC values against the 0-1023 range. Shut down cleanly on SIGINT/SIGTERM by turning off the fan, closing SPI, and releasing pigpio resources.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using libgpiod to monitor a GP2Y0A21YK0F IR distance sensor, read via an MCP3008 ADC on SPI0, CE0, channel 0, at a 1 MHz SPI clock, and control a 5V relay connected to a magnetic door sensor. When proximity is detected (< 20 cm), energize the relay, active-high on GPIO17, to simulate door opening. Use a 100 ms polling interval and a 1 s debounce delay after triggering. Log each event with a timestamp to 'door_events.log'. Include robust error handling for all GPIO, SPI, and file I/O operations, handle sensor-absent or bus-error paths, and cleanly release all resources on all exit paths, including SIGINT.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using the pigpio library to control a proportional solenoid valve (ASCO RedHat 8210 series) connected to GPIO17 (PWM-capable, BCM numbering), modulating its opening based on readings from an analog soil moisture sensor (Vegetronix VH400) connected to an MCP3008 ADC via SPI channel 0 (CE0 on GPIO8), 1 MHz clock, SPI mode 0. Using pigpio's built-in SPI (spiOpen/spiXfer) with correct MCP3008 single-ended command bytes, read 3 sensors on ADC channels 0-2, average the readings, and map the average (0-1023) inversely to valve opening (0-100%): dry soil (low ADC value) gives high opening, wet soil (high ADC value) gives low opening. Set the PWM frequency to 100 Hz with range 100 for 0-100% duty cycle. Log the timestamp, the 3 raw ADC values, the average, and the valve position to 'irrigation.log' every 5 seconds. Check pigpio init, SPI open, every SPI transfer, and the log file open; handle individual sensor read failures by skipping them in the average. Use signal handlers (SIGINT, SIGTERM) for graceful shutdown: close the valve (PWM=0), close SPI, close the log file, and terminate pigpio.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W to read soil moisture levels from a YL-69 sensor connected to channel 0 (CH0) of an MCP3008 ADC, interfaced via SPI0 (CE0 on GPIO8) using the pigpio library at 1 MHz in SPI Mode 0. Ensure the SPI command bytes are correctly formatted for the MCP3008 (start bit, single-ended mode, channel 0) and the 10-bit ADC value is extracted correctly; validate the ADC value against the 10-bit range (0-1023) before converting to a moisture percentage. Log readings with timestamps to 'soil_data.txt' every 5 seconds. Handle potential SPI communication errors gracefully with a retry mechanism of up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff; if SPI fails persistently, skip the reading and log an error. Implement graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM, ensuring all SPI handles and pigpio resources are released.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W that synthesizes a Theremin-like instrument using libgpiod for GPIO control and the sysfs PWM interface (/sys/class/pwm/) for audio generation. Map the distance reading from a single HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor (Trig on GPIO23, Echo on GPIO24) to audio frequency from 220 Hz to 880 Hz, and control the volume (PWM duty cycle on GPIO18, PWM0) using a photoresistor (LDR) read via an MCP3008 ADC over SPI0. Handle sensor read errors, such as timeouts and SPI failures, gracefully by holding the last valid state, manage all resources cleanly on SIGINT, and save and load calibration data to 'theremin_config.txt'.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ using the pigpio library to monitor an MQ-135 air quality sensor (analog output) via an MCP3008 ADC over SPI (channel 0, 1 MHz, mode 0), reading MCP3008 channel 0 (single-ended) every 5 seconds. Convert the ADC value (0-1023) to an AQI using a linear mapping (0-500). Control a 12V ventilation fan connected to GPIO18 (BCM) via a relay: turn it on when AQI > 100, off otherwise. Log the timestamp and AQI to 'air_quality.log' in append mode. Use the proper MCP3008 SPI protocol: start bit (0x01), single-ended mode (0x08), channel select (0x00-0x07), then read the 10-bit result from response bytes 1 and 2. Implement robust error handling for SPI communication failures, including retry logic and re-initialization: on SPI read failure, retry up to 3 times with a 1-second delay; if still failing, re-initialize SPI and continue. Handle SIGINT/SIGTERM for graceful shutdown (fan off, close SPI, close log, terminate pigpio), and ensure all resources are released on exit paths.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using the libgpiod library (not bcm2835 or wiringPi) for any GPIO control and standard Linux spidev for SPI communication with an MCP3008 ADC, to read analog voltage from an MQ-3 alcohol sensor connected to MCP3008 channel 0 via SPI0 (CE0 on GPIO8), channel 0 single-ended mode, 1 MHz SPI clock, SPI mode 0, 8 bits per word. Sample every 1 second with ISO 8601 UTC timestamps and log readings to 'alcohol_log.txt'. Send the MCP3008 command as tx[0]=0x01 (start), tx[1]=(channel<<4)|0x80 (single-ended + channel), tx[2]=0x00, and compute result = ((rx[1] & 0x03) << 8) | rx[2]. Convert ADC values (0-1023) to approximate PPM using PPM = (adc_value * 0.5) - 10.0. Classify readings: above 50 PPM as 'Alcohol detected! Limit exceeded.', below 20 PPM as 'Sobriety confirmed.', and between as 'Alcohol level within acceptable range.'. Handle ADC read errors robustly by validating SPI transfers and detecting sensor-absent conditions (ADC reads 0 or 1023 consistently) and reporting them; retry failed SPI reads up to 3 times with a 100 ms delay before logging an error. Check all syscall return values and handle errors with descriptive messages. Handle SIGINT/SIGTERM for graceful shutdown, closing all file descriptors and releasing GPIO resources.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B using the pigpio library to read analog soil moisture data from a DFROBOT Soil Moisture Sensor connected via SPI to an 8-channel, 10-bit MCP3008 ADC. The sensor's analog output is connected to MCP3008 channel 0 (CH0). The MCP3008 is wired to SPI0: CE0 on GPIO8, SCLK on GPIO11, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9, at SPI mode 0, 1 MHz clock. When the moisture reading falls below a threshold of 300 (out of 1023), activate a 12V water pump via a relay controlled by GPIO18 (active high). Log each sensor reading and pump status (ON/OFF) with a timestamp to 'irrigation.log' in append mode. The program must run indefinitely, sampling every 60 seconds. Check all pigpio initializations, SPI opens, and file opens; handle sensor read failures gracefully by logging the error and continuing. On SIGINT or SIGTERM, turn off the pump, close SPI, close the log file, and terminate pigpio cleanly. Use only the pigpio API (no wiringPi).

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to independently control two Adafruit Mini DC Motors with wires (Product ID: 155) using the pigpio library: Motor 1 enable on GPIO18, direction on GPIO23; Motor 2 enable on GPIO24, direction on GPIO25. Read the speed of each motor from a potentiometer via an MCP3008 ADC over SPI (SPI channel 0, 1 MHz, mode 0; MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9, SCLK on GPIO11, CE0 on GPIO8), with Potentiometer 1 on ADC channel 0 and Potentiometer 2 on ADC channel 1. Map the 10-bit potentiometer values (0-1023) to speed factors using a logarithmic function for finer low-speed control, then run a motion profile that moves Motor 1 forward and Motor 2 backward simultaneously (or sequentially with a short delay), accelerating from MIN_SPEED (50) to MAX_SPEED (255) scaled by the speed factor, holding constant speed for 2 seconds, then decelerating back to MIN_SPEED; after a 5-second pause, reverse directions and repeat. Use pigpio's gpioPWM for speed control and gpioWrite for direction. Include robust error handling for all pigpio and SPI operations, handle sensor-absent or bus-error paths gracefully, and release all resources (PWM, SPI, GPIO) on exit, including via signal handlers for SIGINT and SIGTERM.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to continuously sample sound levels from an Adafruit MAX9814 Electret Microphone Amplifier, whose analog AOUT output is connected to channel 0 of a 10-bit MCP3008 ADC (CS on GPIO8, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9, SCLK on GPIO11), using pigpio's spiOpen/spiXfer for SPI communication, with samples ranging 0-1023. Calibrate for 5 seconds at startup to establish the average ambient level, then trigger an LED on GPIO17 when the sound level exceeds the calibrated noise threshold of 10% above average ambient, using a 10 ms debounce on LED activation to prevent rapid toggling. Include robust error handling: check pigpio initialization, SPI handle creation, and GPIO modes. Handle SIGINT for graceful cleanup: turn the LED off, close the SPI handle, and terminate pigpio.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to interface with a Honeywell AWM720P airflow sensor using its analog voltage output via an MCP3008 ADC (SPI channel 0, CE0, 1 MHz), using the pigpio library (not wiringPi) for SPI and a pigpio timer. The sensor outputs 0.5V at 0 SLPM and 4.5V at 200 SLPM (linear); sample the voltage every 100 ms and convert to airflow in SLPM using airflow = (voltage - 0.5) / (4.5 - 0.5) * 200. Log each reading with a timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) to 'airflow_log.txt' in append mode. Handle ADC read errors gracefully by logging "ERROR: ADC read failed" with a timestamp and continuing. Include robust error handling for all initialization steps (pigpio, SPI, file open) and release resources on all exit paths. On SIGINT (Ctrl+C), close the SPI handle, close the log file, and terminate pigpio. The program should run indefinitely until interrupted.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W using libgpiod v2 and spidev to sample analog audio from an ADMP401 MEMS microphone via a 10-bit MCP3008 SPI ADC. The ADMP401 analog output connects to MCP3008 CH0 (pin 1). Wiring: CS to GPIO8 (CE0, physical pin 24), MOSI to GPIO10 (physical pin 19), MISO to GPIO9 (physical pin 21), SCLK to GPIO11 (physical pin 23), VDD to 3.3V, VREF to 3.3V. Use /dev/spidev0.0 at SPI mode 0, 8 bits/word, 1 MHz max speed. Sample at 1000 Hz (1 ms period), sleeping until the next sample deadline with nanosleep. For each sample, manually control CS using libgpiod v2 (request GPIO8 as output, drive low before the transfer, high after), send the 3-byte MCP3008 single-ended channel-0 command (start bit 0x01, config byte (0x08|channel)<<4, dummy 0x00), and parse the 10-bit result from rx_buf[1..2]. Log each reading as "timestamp_ns|raw_adc_value\n" to 'audio_log.txt', using clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW) for nanosecond timestamps and flushing after each write. Handle SPI open/ioctl failures, GPIO chip/line request failures, file open/write/flush failures, and signals (SIGINT, SIGTERM) for graceful shutdown, releasing the GPIO line request, closing the SPI fd, and closing the log file on all exit paths. Validate all return codes. Do not use sysfs GPIO or wiringPi, and include <stdint.h> for uint8_t/uint32_t types.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to read the analog voltage from a Honeywell MICROpeL MP-741 Combustible Gas Sensor via an MCP3008 ADC connected over SPI (CE0, channel 0), using the pigpio library (not wiringPi) at 1 MHz SPI clock, reading MCP3008 channel 0 in single-ended mode. Convert the 10-bit ADC value to voltage using VREF = 3.3 V, then calculate PPM using the placeholder linear relationship PPM = voltage * 1000.0 (no actual calibration). Log the timestamp, voltage, and PPM to 'gas_log.txt' in append mode, and print the voltage and PPM to the console every second. Check SPI initialization, SPI transfer failures, and file open errors; on ADC read failure, retry after a 100 ms delay. Use a signal handler (SIGINT) to close SPI and terminate pigpio cleanly, with proper resource cleanup on all exit paths. Simulate a propane leak detector with continuous operation until Ctrl+C.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to read X, Y, and Z acceleration values from an ADXL335 analog accelerometer. Since the ADXL335 is analog, read its voltages using the pigpio library for SPI communication and GPIO control via an MCP3008 10-bit ADC (SPI mode 0, 8 channels, reference voltage 3.3V): ADXL335 X-out to MCP3008 CH0, Y-out to CH1, Z-out to CH2; MCP3008 CS to GPIO8, MOSI to GPIO10, MISO to GPIO9, SCLK to GPIO11. The ADXL335 has a sensitivity of 300 mV/g and a zero-g bias of 1.5V; scale the ADC readings accordingly. Apply a Kalman filter to smooth the data from each axis and print the filtered acceleration values (in g) to the console at a rate of 10 Hz. Check every initialization and SPI transaction, and handle sensor-absent and bus-error paths gracefully. Ensure clean resource release on all exit paths, including proper signal handling for both SIGINT and SIGTERM before the program terminates.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ to read three Texas Instruments DRV5055VA Hall-Effect sensors using the libgpiod C API (v0.3.x legacy API; not sysfs or wiringPi), connected to GPIO4, GPIO17, and GPIO27, using individual gpiod_line_request_input() calls (not bulk request functions) for broad compatibility. Since the Raspberry Pi lacks a hardware ADC, simulate the analog-to-digital conversion by reading the digital logic state of each pin (HIGH = 3.3V, LOW = 0.0V) and treating it as the sensor output. Calculate the magnetic field strength in millitesla using B = (V_out - V_quiescent) / Sensitivity, with VCC = 3.3V so V_quiescent = 1.65V and a sensitivity of 0.025 V/mT (25 mV/mT). Sample every 100 milliseconds and log the readings to 'magnetic_log.txt' in comma-separated format (e.g., 'sensor1_mT,sensor2_mT,sensor3_mT'), flushing the file after each write. Print a warning to stderr if any computed magnetic field value falls outside the range -100 mT to +100 mT. On any GPIO read error, skip logging for that iteration and continue. Handle SIGINT (Ctrl+C) for graceful shutdown, properly releasing all libgpiod resources, with robust error handling for GPIO access and file I/O throughout.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B using the pigpio library to read analog soil moisture sensor data from an MCP3008 ADC (channel 0, single-ended mode, SPI CE0, 500 kHz, mode 0). The sensor output range is 0 (dry) to 1023 (wet). If the moisture level falls below 30%, turn on a 12V water pump relay connected to GPIO17 (active high); if moisture rises to 30% or above, turn off the pump. Log all events, program start, pump on/off, errors, and termination, with timestamps to 'watering.log'. Check every pigpio and SPI call, and handle ADC read failures gracefully by logging the error and continuing. Ensure the pump is off on exit, using a signal handler (SIGINT, SIGTERM) for clean shutdown. Use only pigpio (not wiringPi). The program should run indefinitely, checking every 60 seconds.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ using the libgpiod library (not wiringPi) to log ADC readings from an MCP3008 connected via SPI0, CE0 on single-ended channels 0, 1, and 2 to a CSV file named 'sensor_data.csv', simulating a soil moisture monitoring system logging moisture levels from three different locations. Initialize SPI using the spidev interface: open /dev/spidev0.0, set mode SPI_MODE_0, 8 bits per word, 1 MHz speed. Read each channel by sending the 3-byte command: start bit (0x01), then single-ended mode byte with channel select (0x80 | (channel<<4)), then a dummy byte (0x00); the returned 10-bit value is ((data[1] & 0x03) << 8) | data[2]. Log data every 1 second. Check every open/ioctl/read/write call; on failure print an error message and exit gracefully. Handle SIGINT (Ctrl+C) to close the CSV file and release SPI resources before exiting. Use only modern Linux APIs; do not use wiringPi or pigpio.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that subscribes to the MQTT topic "home/led_control" on broker mqtt.eclipseprojects.io:1883 with client ID "rpi_led_control" and QoS 0, to receive JSON payloads containing an "led_state" boolean, and uses the pigpio library to control an LED connected to GPIO17. Initialize pigpio, set GPIO17 as output, and turn off the LED on startup. Parse JSON payloads expecting exactly the key "led_state" with a boolean value, rejecting any other keys or invalid types; on a valid message, set GPIO17 HIGH if led_state is true, LOW if false. Handle disconnections gracefully with exponential backoff reconnection (1s, 2s, 4s, ... up to a 60s maximum delay). Use signal handlers (SIGINT, SIGTERM) for clean shutdown: disconnect MQTT, turn off the LED, and release pigpio resources, ensuring all resources are released on every exit path (success, error, signal). Log all errors to stderr with timestamps. Use only pigpio (gpioInitialise, gpioSetMode, gpioWrite, gpioTerminate), mosquitto with v2 callbacks via mosquitto_loop_start/stop, and cJSON for parsing; do not use any other sensors or peripherals (no ADC, no IMU, no vibration motor, no file logging).

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B using the libgpiod library (not wiringPi) for GPIO control, to read a KY-038 sound sensor module whose digital output (DO) pin is connected to GPIO17 (BCM numbering) and goes LOW when sound exceeds the onboard-potentiometer threshold, and to trigger a simulated alarm LED on GPIO18. Print the sound level reading (0 or 1) to the console each loop iteration, with a 100 ms delay between readings. When sound is detected (DO = LOW), blink the LED on GPIO18 for 1 second: ON for 1 s, then OFF. Check libgpiod initialization, chip open, line request, and all I/O operations; handle sensor-absent or bus-error paths gracefully, printing an error and exiting if the chip open fails. On SIGINT (Ctrl+C) or SIGTERM, cleanly release all GPIO lines and exit, with proper resource cleanup on all exit paths.

Create a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that monitors an SW-420 vibration sensor connected to GPIO17 (physical pin 11). The sensor module's DO pin is active-low, open-collector: it idles HIGH and pulls LOW when vibration exceeds the onboard-potentiometer threshold. Use libgpiod (not sysfs, not wiringPi) to open /dev/gpiochip0, obtain GPIO line 17, and request it for falling-edge event detection with the consumer label "vibration-monitor", using the single-line event API (gpiod_line_event_wait / gpiod_line_event_read, not struct gpiod_line_bulk) so the code builds against libgpiod v1.x headers. Install handlers for SIGINT and SIGTERM that set a volatile sig_atomic_t flag so the main loop can exit cleanly. On each falling-edge event, read it with gpiod_line_event_read, append a timestamped line to /var/log/vibration_shutdown.log (opened in append mode, with error checking on fopen/fprintf/fclose), print the same message to stdout, then invoke system("sudo shutdown -h now"). Robustly check every libgpiod call (chip open, get line, request, event wait, event read) and every file I/O call, reporting failures via perror, and clean up all resources (release the line, close the chip) on every exit path.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B to read altitude data from a BMP280 sensor via I2C bus 1 (SDA=GPIO2/pin3, SCL=GPIO3/pin5) at address 0x76 (SDO tied to GND), using the pigpio library. The sensor operates at 3.3V logic — never use 5V. Initialize pigpio and verify the BMP280 chip ID register (0xD0 must return 0x58) before proceeding. Read the 24-byte calibration block from registers 0x88-0xA1 and apply the Bosch compensation formulas, since raw ADC values are meaningless without compensation. Configure ctrl_meas (0xF4) for temperature oversampling x1, pressure oversampling x1, and normal mode. Every 5 seconds, read raw pressure (0xF7-0xF9) and temperature (0xFA-0xFC), compensate them, and compute altitude using the barometric formula with a sea-level pressure of 101325 Pa.
